formation.title: The Birth of Italy
formation.text:
At last, the Italian peninsula stands united under a single banner. For centuries, the land of Dante, Machiavelli, and da Vinci was fractured among warring city-states, foreign overlords, and papal territories. Now that fragmentation is ended.

But unity raises a fundamental question: what kind of Italy shall this be? The peninsula's traditions pull in two directions. One path leads toward a centralized kingdom, a modern nation-state with uniform laws, a national army, and a single capital, modeled on the great powers of Europe. The other path honors the Italian genius for civic self-governance, the commune tradition that created Florence, Venice, and Genoa, each a republic of unprecedented wealth and culture.

The choice will shape Italy's destiny for generations.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: One nation, indivisible: forge the Kingdom of Italy.

modifiers.name: Patria Unita
modifiers.text: Italy has been forged into a single nation-state under centralized rule. The dream of Mazzini and Garibaldi has become reality, one people, one government, one destiny.

options.text: A republic of great cities: let each contribute its genius.

modifiers.name: Repubblica delle Città
modifiers.text: Italy has embraced its heritage as a constellation of great cities (Venice, Florence, Milan, Naples) each contributing its genius to a federated republic that prizes liberty, commerce, and learning above all.

advances.name: Communal Governance
advances.text: The Italian commune, a self-governing urban republic, is one of the most distinctive political innovations of the medieval world. Cities like Florence, Siena, and Lucca developed sophisticated systems of elected councils, written constitutions, and civic magistrates.

advances.name: Maritime Republics
advances.text: Venice, Genoa, Pisa, and Amalfi, the four maritime republics whose merchant fleets and war galleys dominated Mediterranean trade for centuries, establishing trading posts and colonies from the Black Sea to the Atlantic.

advances.name: Guelf and Ghibelline
advances.text: The great factional struggle between papal Guelfs and imperial Ghibellines shaped Italian politics for two centuries, forging a tradition of fierce civic loyalty and political sophistication born from constant negotiation between competing powers.

advances.name: Florentine Banking
advances.text: The great banking houses of Florence (the Medici, Bardi, and Peruzzi) invented modern finance: bills of exchange, double-entry bookkeeping, and international branch networks that moved capital across Europe.

event.title: The Bankers of Florence
event.text:
In the counting houses of Florence, a revolution in finance has transformed the way Europe does business. The great banking families (the Medici, the Bardi, the Peruzzi, the Strozzi) have invented instruments of credit that make it possible to move wealth across vast distances without ever touching a gold coin.

Bills of exchange, letters of credit, and the sistema di partita doppia, double-entry bookkeeping, allow Italian bankers to track every transaction with mathematical precision. Their branch networks stretch from London to Constantinople, and the florin has become the currency of international trade. Kings and popes alike depend on Italian credit to finance their ambitions.

options.text: The wealth of nations flows through our banks.

advances.name: Italian Silk Trade
advances.text: The silk workshops of Lucca, Florence, and Venice produced fabrics of legendary quality, combining raw silk imported from the East with Italian dyeing and weaving techniques to create the most sought-after textiles in Europe.

advances.name: Condottiero Tradition
advances.text: The condottieri, professional mercenary captains and their companies, transformed Italian warfare into a sophisticated art. Leaders like Sforza, Colleoni, and Hawkwood commanded armies of armored lancers and crossbowmen under contract to the highest-bidding city-state.

advances.name: Venetian Shipcraft
advances.text: The Arsenale of Venice was the largest industrial complex in the pre-industrial world, capable of producing a fully equipped warship in a single day. Its assembly-line methods anticipated the Industrial Revolution by four centuries.

event.title: The Arsenal of the Republic
event.text:
The great arsenals of Italy have reached an apex of productivity. In Venice, the Arsenale, stretching across forty-five hectares of the city's eastern shore, can outfit a complete war galley in a single day, an industrial feat unmatched anywhere in Europe. Sixteen thousand arsenalotti labor within its walls, organized into specialized guilds of sawyers, caulkers, oar-makers, and rope-spinners.

This tradition of industrial shipbuilding has spread to other Italian ports. Genoa, Naples, and Livorno have all established their own arsenals, each learning from the Venetian model. The question now is how to deploy this maritime capability.

options.text: Expand the fleet: the Mediterranean is our sea.

modifiers.name: Arsenale Naval Supremacy
modifiers.text: The great arsenals of Italy produce war galleys at a pace unmatched in the Mediterranean, and our captains know how to use them.

options.text: Invest in merchant shipping: commerce is our strength.

modifiers.name: Arsenale Merchant Fleet
modifiers.text: The Italian shipbuilding tradition has been turned toward commerce, producing a merchant fleet that carries goods from the Levant to Flanders.

advances.name: Humanist Learning
advances.text: The studia humanitatis (the study of classical Latin and Greek texts, rhetoric, history, and moral philosophy) began in Italy with Petrarch and Boccaccio, creating an intellectual movement that reshaped European civilization.

advances.name: Galleass Warfare
advances.text: The galleass, developed in the Venetian Arsenal, was a revolutionary warship mounting heavy broadside artillery above banks of oars. At the Battle of Lepanto in 1571, six Venetian galleasses shattered the Ottoman fleet formation before the fleets even closed.

event.title: The Galleass at War
event.text:
Italian naval engineers have perfected the galleass, a revolutionary warship that combines the maneuverability of the galley with the firepower of a sailing warship. These floating fortresses, mounting heavy guns on a continuous deck above the rowers, can deliver devastating broadsides while maintaining the ability to operate in the shallow, wind-fickle waters of the Mediterranean.

At the great Battle of Lepanto in 1571, six Venetian galleasses anchored the Christian line, their concentrated artillery fire shattering the Ottoman formation before the fleets even closed to boarding range. The galleass has proven that firepower, not just ramming and boarding, can decide a naval engagement.

options.text: Our ships are the walls of Italy.

advances.name: Murano Glasscraft
advances.text: The glassmakers of Murano, sequestered on their island to protect trade secrets, developed techniques of unmatched sophistication (cristallo glass, millefiori, lattimo) that made Venetian glass the most prized luxury good in Europe.

advances.name: Commedia dell'Arte
advances.text: The Italian theatrical tradition of improvised comedy, with its stock characters (Arlecchino, Colombina, Pantalone, the Dottore) swept across Europe, establishing Italian performers as the continent's most celebrated entertainers.

advances.name: Palazzo Civic Tradition
advances.text: The palazzo pubblico, the civic palace, was the architectural expression of Italian communal government. From the Palazzo Vecchio in Florence to the Doge's Palace in Venice, these buildings housed councils, courts, and archives that administered the most sophisticated urban governments in Europe.

advances.name: Counter-Reformation
advances.text: Italy stood at the heart of the Catholic Counter-Reformation. The Council of Trent (1545-1563), the founding of the Jesuits, and the Roman Inquisition all emanated from Italian soil, reasserting Catholic orthodoxy and launching a campaign of spiritual renewal.

advances.name: Porto Franco
advances.text: In 1591 and 1593 Grand Duke Ferdinando I issued the Livornine, inviting merchants of every nation (Levantines, Spaniards, Portuguese, Greeks, Germans, Jews, Turks, Moors, Armenians and Persians) to settle at Livorno with freedom of worship and of trade. A fishing village became one of the great ports of the Mediterranean, and Genoa answered with a free port of its own.

advances.name: Accademia Tradition
advances.text: Italy pioneered the modern academy: the Accademia della Crusca standardized the Italian language, the Accademia dei Lincei advanced natural science (counting Galileo among its members), and countless artistic academies trained Europe's finest painters and sculptors.

advances.name: The Grand Tour
advances.text: By the 18th century, no European gentleman's education was complete without a Grand Tour of Italy. The ruins of Rome, the art of Florence, the music of Naples, and the canals of Venice drew thousands of wealthy travelers, making Italy the cultural capital of the civilized world.

advances.name: Enlightened Reforms
advances.text: Italian Enlightenment thinkers (Cesare Beccaria's 'On Crimes and Punishments,' Gaetano Filangieri's 'Science of Legislation') reshaped European thinking about justice, governance, and the rights of the individual. Their ideas influenced reformers from Catherine the Great to Thomas Jefferson.

advances.name: Risorgimento
advances.text: The great movement for Italian national unification (driven by Mazzini's idealism, Garibaldi's military genius, and Cavour's diplomatic cunning) transformed a 'geographical expression' into a nation-state. The Bersaglieri, elite light infantry with their distinctive plumed hats, became its symbol.

event.title: The Risorgimento
event.text:
A great awakening sweeps across the Italian peninsula. In secret lodges and public squares, in pamphlets and poetry, the dream of Italian nationhood has caught fire. Giuseppe Mazzini's 'Young Italy' movement has planted the seed; now it bears fruit in the form of a mass political movement that transcends the old boundaries of kingdom and duchy.

The Carbonari conspirators, the volunteers of Garibaldi's Red Shirts, the diplomatic cunning of Cavour: all have converged toward a single purpose. The foreign yoke is thrown off, the petty principalities dissolved. Italy, the land that gave the world the Renaissance and Roman law, now reclaims its place among the great nations.

This is a moment that demands a vision for the future.

options.text: March on! Italia irredenta must be reclaimed.

modifiers.name: Italia Irredenta March
modifiers.text: The fires of national awakening burn across the peninsula. Volunteers flock to the banner of a united Italy, marching to reclaim every inch of Italian-speaking territory.

options.text: Build the nation: schools, railways, and institutions.

modifiers.name: Nation Building
modifiers.text: The dream of Italian nationhood has been won on the battlefield; now it must be cemented through schools, railways, and institutions that bind the peninsula into a true nation.

advances.name: Carbonari Networks
advances.text: The Carbonari, 'charcoal burners', were Italy's most influential secret revolutionary society. Operating through coded rituals and clandestine cells across the peninsula, they organized uprisings against foreign rule and planted the seeds of Italian nationalism.

advances.name: Industrial Awakening
advances.text: Piedmont and Lombardy led Italy's industrial transformation: Cavour's railway-building program, the Ansaldo steelworks of Genoa, and the textile mills of the Po Valley brought modern industry to a land long defined by agriculture and artisanship.

advances.name: National Education
advances.text: The Casati Law of 1859 and the subsequent educational reforms created a unified Italian school system, combating the peninsula's extreme regional illiteracy and building a shared national identity through the teaching of standard Italian.

advances.name: Italia Irredenta
advances.text: The doctrine of Italia Irredenta, 'unredeemed Italy', demanded the incorporation of all Italian-speaking territories, particularly Trentino, Trieste, Istria, and Dalmatia, into the Italian state, driving diplomatic ambition and military planning.

destiny.name: The Italian Destiny
destiny.text: Italy stands united, but unity is merely the beginning. The peninsula that gave the world Rome, the Renaissance, and the foundations of modern civilization must now choose its future among the great powers. Stabilize the new nation and chart your course.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Italian Destiny
event.text:
The dream of Italian unity has been achieved. From the Alps to Sicily, from the Ligurian coast to the Adriatic shore, the peninsula is one. But the great question remains: what shall Italy become?

The foundations are laid. Now we must build upon them, with purpose, with ambition, and with the knowledge that we are the heirs of Rome and the Renaissance both. The future of the Mediterranean, perhaps of Europe itself, turns upon the choices we make in this decisive hour.

destiny.name: Italia Irredenta
destiny.text: The terre irredente (Trieste, Trento, and the Italian-speaking lands still under foreign rule) must be reclaimed. Assemble an army worthy of the cause and march to liberate every inch of Italian soil.

conditions.text: Chose the Patria Unita destiny
Own Trieste, or a subject owns it
Own Trent, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 30

event.title: The Unredeemed Lands
event.text:
The tricolore flies over Trieste and Trento at last. For decades, Italian patriots spoke of the terre irredente, the unredeemed lands where Italian was spoken but foreign flags flew. Now they are Italian.

The army that accomplished this feat has been tempered in the crucible of irredentist warfare. Our soldiers know what it means to fight for national honor, and the general staff has proven its capacity for combined-arms operations against a European great power. Italy has announced its arrival on the stage of history.

options.text: Every inch of Italian soil is ours.

destiny.name: The Fourth Shore
destiny.text: The Mediterranean's southern shore, Tunisia and Tripolitania, once fed the Roman Empire. Take Tunis and Tripoli across the sea, and Italy can establish its African empire and control the central Mediterranean.

conditions.text: Own Tunis, or a subject owns it
Own Tripoli, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Fourth Shore
event.text:
Italian boots tread the sands of North Africa. Tunisia and Tripolitania, lands that once formed the breadbasket of the Roman Empire, now fall under the Italian flag. The Mediterranean is no longer a barrier but a bridge, connecting the mother country to its new African provinces.

But an overseas empire demands choices. Some argue for rapid military buildup, conscripting colonial regiments, establishing garrisons, and preparing for the next war of expansion. Others see the value of naval dominance, controlling the sea lanes that connect Italy to its new possessions, and projecting power through the fleet rather than the barracks.

options.text: Raise the legions: Africa needs soldiers.

modifiers.name: Legioni Africane
modifiers.text: Italy's African legions, colonial regiments recruited, trained, and garrisoned to hold the Fourth Shore and prepare for further expansion across the Mediterranean littoral.

options.text: Command the sea: the fleet is our strength.

modifiers.name: Dominio dei Mari
modifiers.text: The Italian fleet rules the waves between Sicily and the African coast, projecting power through naval dominance rather than garrisons, a maritime strategy worthy of the Venetian and Genoese tradition.

destiny.name: Mare Nostrum
destiny.text: Mare Nostrum, Our Sea. From Thessaloniki to Alexandria, from Smyrna to the Strait of Messina, Italy must command the entire Mediterranean basin. Only then will the heirs of Rome have truly restored the imperium.

conditions.text: Own Thessaloníki, or a subject owns it
Own Smyrna, or a subject owns it
Own Alexandria, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75

event.title: Mare Nostrum
event.text:
Mare Nostrum, Our Sea. The words of the ancient Romans ring true once more. From Malta to the shores of Egypt, from Thessaloniki to the coasts of Libya, the Italian flag commands respect across the breadth of the Mediterranean.

This is not merely an empire of territory but an empire of influence, of trade routes and chokepoints, of cultural prestige and military power. Italy has achieved what no Italian state has accomplished since the fall of Rome: dominion over the inner sea.

The question now is how to wield this power. Some urge a new Roman imperium, centralized authority, mass levies, and the diplomatic weight of a true great power. Others advocate a fortress strategy, making Italy's Mediterranean positions impregnable through the trace italienne fortifications that Italian engineers pioneered.

modifiers.name: Novum Imperium Romanum
modifiers.text: A new Roman Empire, Italy wields the aggressive military power of a true Mediterranean hegemon, projecting force rapidly across its dominions, though the strain of perpetual campaigning takes its toll.

options.text: Fortify every position: Italy is impregnable.

modifiers.name: Traccia Italiana
modifiers.text: The trace italienne, angular bastion fortifications pioneered by Italian military engineers, makes every Italian position across the Mediterranean an impregnable stronghold defended by modern artillery.

destiny.name: Stato da Mar
destiny.text: The Venetian Stato da Mar, the maritime state, was built on Adriatic trade supremacy. Secure Ragusa, ensure Italian silk flows through our markets, and lay the foundation for a commercial empire that rivals the Serenissima.

event.title: The Stato da Mar
event.text:
The Lion of Saint Mark once flew over the trading posts of the Adriatic and the fortresses of the Ionian shore. Now Italy inherits that legacy, not as a single maritime republic but as a confederation of great cities, each contributing its genius to a shared commercial destiny.

Venetian merchants handle the spice trade, Genoese bankers finance the ventures, Florentine workshops transform raw silk into fine cloth, and Neapolitan shipwrights build the galleys that carry it all. The Dominio da Mar lives again, an Italian Mediterranean where commerce is king.

destiny.name: Banca d'Italia
destiny.text: Italian banking must reclaim the preeminence of the Medici era. Secure Crete as the central Mediterranean's key waypoint, fill the treasury, and raise Florence, the city of the Bardi, the Peruzzi and the Medici, to 56 development.

conditions.text: Own Candia, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000
We own Florence and its development is at least 56

event.title: The Banca d'Italia
event.text:
Italian banking has reclaimed its ancient preeminence. The tradition of the Medici and the Bardi lives on in a modern form, a unified Italian banking system that commands the flow of capital across Europe. Bills of exchange drawn on Italian houses are honored from London to Constantinople, and the gold reserves of the Banca d'Italia rival those of any nation.

With Crete secured, the central Mediterranean's greatest waypoint, Italian commercial networks now stretch unbroken from the western Mediterranean to the Levant. The question is how to leverage this financial power.

options.text: Diplomacy and influence: the Medici way.

modifiers.name: Diplomazia Medicea
modifiers.text: The Medici way, influence through finance, diplomacy through generosity, power through the cultivation of friends. Italian ambassadors are welcomed in every court, and Italian credit opens every door.

options.text: Monopolize the routes: control the trade.

modifiers.name: Monopolio delle Rotte
modifiers.text: Italian merchants and bankers have cornered the most profitable trade routes in the Mediterranean, extracting wealth from every transaction; though such aggressive commerce drives prices upward.

destiny.name: Rinascimento Universale
destiny.text: A universal renaissance: Italy as the wealthiest and most commercially connected nation in the world. Found an Arts Academy in the capital, as Florence gathered its painters and sculptors in the Accademia del Disegno, fill the coffers, and rebuild Rome as the popes of the first Renaissance began to, until the city of ruins and pasture is a capital again. Requires an Arts Academy in the capital, Rome at 63 development and 3,000 gold.

conditions.text: We own Rome and its development is at least 63
The capital
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Universal Renaissance
event.text:
The numbers do not lie. Italian cities lead the world in population, in wealth, in the production of goods both fine and common. Italian banks command the flow of capital from the Baltic to the Levant. Italian institutions of learning set the standard that all others aspire to reach.

This is no mere prosperity. It is a second Renaissance. Where the first Rinascimento revived the arts and letters of antiquity, this Rinascimento Universale has created something new: a civilization of commerce, culture, and innovation that radiates outward from the Italian peninsula to transform the world. The question now is how to sustain this golden age.

options.text: Invest in knowledge: ideas are eternal.

modifiers.name: Rinascimento Universale
modifiers.text: A universal rebirth, Italian institutions, academies, and workshops drive the advancement of human knowledge, attracting talent from across the world and ensuring that ideas born in Italy reshape civilization.

modifiers.name: Crocevia dei Continenti
modifiers.text: Italy stands at the crossroads of continents, a cosmopolitan commercial empire where diverse peoples are welcomed, infrastructure is built to last, and the loyalty of subjects is earned through prosperity rather than force.

units.name: Condottiero Lances
units.text: Heavy cavalry in the condottiero tradition, these armored lancers serve under contract and are renowned for their devastating charges and tactical flexibility.

units.name: Condottiero Lances
units.text: Levy cavalry raised in the Italian condottiero tradition, armored horsemen drawing on centuries of mercenary warfare expertise.

units.name: Galleass
units.text: A massive warship combining oar-power with broadside artillery. Developed in Venice, the galleass mounts heavy cannons on a continuous gun deck above the rowers, delivering devastating firepower while retaining maneuverability in Mediterranean waters.

units.name: Bersaglieri
units.text: Elite light infantry of the Risorgimento era, renowned for their speed, marksmanship, and aggressive tactics. Identified by their distinctive wide-brimmed hats adorned with capercaillie feathers.

buildings.name: Banco
buildings.text: An Italian banking house in the Florentine tradition, facilitating international trade through bills of exchange, letters of credit, and branch networks stretching across Europe.

buildings.name: Setificio
buildings.text: An Italian silk workshop where master weavers transform raw silk and dyes into fine cloth of extraordinary quality, continuing the traditions perfected in Lucca, Florence, and Venice.

buildings.name: Arsenale
buildings.text: A great shipyard complex modeled on the Venetian Arsenal, where thousands of specialized craftsmen produce warships and merchant vessels with an efficiency unmatched in the world.

buildings.name: Palazzo Comunale
buildings.text: A civic palace housing the organs of communal government (elected councils, law courts, and administrative archives) embodying the Italian tradition of urban self-governance.

buildings.name: Porto Franco
buildings.text: A free port: goods may be landed, stored in bonded warehouses and shipped out again without paying duty, and the foreign merchants who handle them live under the protection of the prince with their own consuls, churches and synagogues.

buildings.name: Accademia
buildings.text: An academy of arts and sciences in the Italian tradition, where scholars, artists, and natural philosophers advance human knowledge and refine the Italian language and culture.

buildings.name: Vetreria
buildings.text: A Murano-style glassworks where master craftsmen produce cristallo, millefiori, and lattimo glass using closely guarded Venetian techniques.

buildings.name: Manifattura
buildings.text: An Italian industrial manufactory producing steel and finished goods, representing the industrial transformation that accompanied national unification.

buildings.name: Carbonari Lodge
buildings.text: A clandestine meeting place of the Carbonari revolutionary society, where patriots gather to plot against foreign domination and advance the cause of Italian nationhood.

buildings.name: Fortezza Moderna
buildings.text: A state-of-the-art Italian fortress complex incorporating the trace italienne, the angular bastion design that Italian military engineers pioneered and that revolutionized defensive warfare across Europe.

buildings.name: Conservatorio
buildings.text: An Italian conservatory of music and arts, where composers, musicians, and performers train in the tradition that produced Vivaldi, Monteverdi, and the operatic form that conquered the stages of Europe.

list.name: Consiglio dei Dieci
list.text: Established 25 June 1310 after the failed Tiepolo conspiracy and made permanent in 1335, the Venetian Council of Ten ran the Republic's intelligence service and political-crimes tribunal. Anonymous denunciations slipped through the bocche di leone bypassed the slower Maggior Consiglio, giving the state a swift instrument against treason at the price of patrician resentment.

list.name: Casa di San Giorgio
list.text: Chartered 23 April 1407 to consolidate Genoa's escalating war debts with Venice, the Casa delle compere e dei banchi di San Giorgio managed transferable luoghi shares, the salt monopoly, and the Republic's tax farms. Hailed as the world's first modern public bank, it predated the Bank of England by nearly three centuries and sustained Genoese credit until Napoleon's 1805 suppression.

list.name: Sant'Uffizio
list.text: Pope Paul III's bull Licet ab initio of 21 July 1542 established the Supreme Sacred Congregation of the Roman and Universal Inquisition under Cardinal Carafa. The Holy Office operated through diocesan tribunals across the peninsula, administered the Index of Prohibited Books from 1559, and served as the doctrinal court of the Counter-Reformation.

conditions.text: Catholicism religion

list.name: Arsenale di Venezia
list.text: The Venetian state shipyard, whose present structure dates from 1104 under Doge Ordelafo Faliero, was expanded by the Arsenale Nuovo in 1320. At its early-16th-century peak it employed 16,000 arsenalotti and could fit out a galley a day on a standardized-parts production line, making the Republic's fleet the engine of its commercial empire across the Stato da Mar.

conditions.text: Owns Venice

list.name: Sistema della Condotta
list.text: The Italian capitulation system through which 14th- and 15th-century city-states hired professional condottieri under standardized contracts specifying the ferma (service period), pay, and aspetto (renewal interval). When a condotta lapsed, the captain could not war on his former employer for two years. The system substituted contracted noble captains for civic militias and dominated Italian warfare until Charles VIII's 1494 invasion.

list.name: Accademie
list.text: The learned societies that institutionalised Italian high culture: the Accademia della Crusca, founded in Florence in 1583, fixed the literary vernacular through its 1612 Vocabolario, model for Richelieu's later Academie Francaise; the Accademia dei Lincei, founded in Rome on 17 August 1603 by Prince Federico Cesi, was the world's first scientific academy and counted Galileo Galilei among its early members.

list.name: Parlamento Siciliano
list.text: The Sicilian Parliament, traceable to Roger II's Curia Regis at Mazara in 1130 and codified by Frederick II's 1232 constitutions. Its three brazos, militare (nobles), ecclesiastico (clergy), and demaniale (royal towns), met to grant donativos to the crown. Surviving Aragonese, Spanish, and Bourbon rule until 1816, it was the longest-lived parliamentary institution of the peninsula.
